name: Klammen-Wanderweg Leutasch
beschreibung:
Carving deep into the limestone between Tyrol and Bavaria, the Leutasch Spirit Gorge (Leutascher Geisterklamm) is one of the most spectacular canyon walks in the Eastern Alps. A bold steel walkway anchored directly into sheer vertical cliffs takes visitors up to 43 metres above rushing turquoise waters, revealing dramatic geological forces in action.

Trails & Requirements

The gorge features three distinct sections. The Klammgeistweg (Gorge Spirit Trail, ~3 km) starts at car park P19 in Leutasch-Schanz: an 800-metre steel-mesh gallery suspended along cliff walls leads to a scenic panoramic bridge spanning 45 metres above the chasm, accompanied by folklore storyboards about the gorge spirit.

From the Bavarian side, the Koboldpfad (Goblin Trail, ~1.9 km) climbs from the Mittenwald entrance up to the bridge. The standard Great Gorge Circuit covers approx. 3.2 km with 130 metres of ascent (~1 to 1.5 hours). A full cross-border loop down to Mittenwald reaches approx. 5 km (2 to 2.5 hours). A short historical wooden boardwalk (~200 m) at the Mittenwald kiosk leads directly to a 23-metre waterfall.

Season & Admission: The main elevated walkway and goblin trail are open from early May to late October and are completely free of charge. Only the short wooden waterfall trail at the Mittenwald kiosk charges a small fee (€4 adults, €2 children, cash only). Closed in winter for safety.

Getting There

Main Tyrolean trailhead: Car park P19 Geisterklamm in Schanz (6105 Leutasch). Day parking €6 (card, cash or EasyPark app). By public transport: Take VVT regional bus Line 431 (Telfs – Leutasch – Mittenwald) directly to the stop „Leutasch Geisterklamm“ (free for guests holding the Seefeld PlateauCard).

Tips

  • Families: Excellent for walking children aged 4+ with playful themed stations. Not suitable for pushchairs: Turnstiles, stairs, and metal gratings prevent stroller access – use a baby backpack instead.
  • Dogs: Strongly discouraged: The open metal mesh flooring pinches paws, catches claws, and can cause panic due to the sheer 40 m drop beneath.
  • Footwear: Sturdy footwear with rubber traction is essential on wet metal and wooden walkways.
  • Bicycles: Cycling is strictly prohibited along all gorge walkways.
